content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: overtime for 12 general agents plus break delay and cross-skill moves, lifting service level to 88.0% (target 80%) for ₹3,600.","why":"A 10:50 regional TV ad for the zero-balance savings account pushed general calls to 122–124 per interval against about 79 forecast. New-offer enquiries are at 3.7x normal. Staffing is as planned and there is no IT incident, so this is extra demand, not a shortfall. With no action, the 13:00–16:15 window is predicted at 78.1%, and general sits at only 66.2%. P3 offers overtime to 12 general agents from 13:30 to 15:30. It also delays general breaks 13:00–14:00 by 45 minutes and moves cross-skilled agents between queues. Predicted results for the window are 88.0% overall, general 81.9%, payments 95.1% and abandons 2.3%. It is the only policy-compliant plan that reaches target. Rest of day rises to 91.2%.","trade_offs":["P1 (free rebalance) reaches only 78.3% overall, with general at 66.6%. It misses the target.","P2 and P4 add an IVR outage message for new-offer enquiries. They break policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident. P4 would give 89.6% for the same ₹3,600, but it is not permitted.","Payments is not put at risk: it improves to 95.1% from 91.8% under no action, despite 3 agents moving to general from 15:00 to 16:00.","Cost is ₹3,600 from the remaining overtime budget. This plan uses all 12 overtime offers, so there is little left for further surprises."],"watch":"Check overtime uptake quickly. General is predicted at only 81.9%, so if fewer than 12 agents accept, it could fall below 80%. Also watch for further airings of the ad that could drive another call spike."}
